originalFinding.title: Preserve unknown delivery when project registration fails after directory creation succeeds
originalFinding.trigger: With 127 registered projects, start two different project/create requests before either worker result returns. Both pass the pre-await count check, both cross beforeWrite and create their directory, and both return successful worker acknowledgements. The first addProject consumes slot 128; the second addProject throws HarnessError(capacity) with its default delivery=not_sent.
originalFinding.impact: The second operation is permanently recorded and reported as not_sent even though its directory was already created. It is absent from project/list, the user receives false safe-to-retry guidance, and no project/create positive-proof recovery path repairs this receipt. This violates the explicit not_sent versus unknown contract.
evidence: The standalone reproduction imports transformed current frozen source and uses a real in-memory SQLite Ledger, a barrier to order two positive worker acknowledgements, and actual mkdir under .work.

.work/v230-gateway-project-create-repro/proof.json: first request accepted; second request rejected with code=capacity and delivery=not_sent; second persisted receipt state=not_sent; both directoryExists=true; registeredProjects=128.

The handler catches this locally raised HarnessError through errorBody(error, unknown), but errorBody preserves the error delivery field and therefore ignores the fallback after the acknowledged side effect.
originalFinding.relatedSameCause: The same post-success classification can be reached through object(created) or validText(created.path). Worktree receipt projection accepts identifier(worktreeId), while later Worktrees.apply calls uuid(worktreeId); malformed positive worker data there can likewise raise a default not_sent during local postprocessing. These are the same delivery-boundary defect, not separately counted findings; the concurrency case above is the dynamically confirmed trigger.
originalFinding.recommendation: Track positive backend acknowledgement separately from dispatch and never downgrade a subsequent local postprocessing failure to not_sent. Preserve bounded recovery information and actionable guidance for a created-but-unregistered project. Optionally reserve or serialize project-registration capacity across creation/addition/worktree paths, while retaining the existing local project/rename transaction rollback exception.

findingDisposition.reason: Positive worker/manager write acknowledgements are recorded before projection or registration; subsequent local failure retains unknown delivery and cannot authorize replaying the backend mutation. Failed project creation registration includes the confirmed path and instructions to add the existing directory.

acceptBackend sets backendAcknowledged before recordDispatch, including adapters without beforeWrite; generic worker mutations, manager writes and project/create all use this boundary.

Catch forces unknown delivery after positive acknowledgement, including default not_sent HarnessError from project result validation, receipt projection, or worktree identity registration; a definite backend rejection before positive acknowledgement remains not_sent.
project/resolve remains read-only and does not set backendAcknowledged; project/add still rechecks authorization/connection at its local mutation boundary.
Local project/rename remains outside the backend acknowledgement path; transaction rollback with original pending row still proves not_sent.

project/create registration failure returns project_registration_failed/unknown with validated created path and add-existing-directory instructions; malformed positive results do not fabricate a usable confirmed path.
